title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Prohibiting the Hierarchical Transfer of Liability to the Superior Organization of the Actor When Taking Civil Compulsory Measures
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Not Changing the Subject of Civil Compulsory Measures to Hold the Superior Institution of the Actor Liable at Each Level

Fa [2004] No. 127

High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

In recent times, some local courts, in cases where banks and non-bank financial institutions (hereinafter referred to as financial institutions) are judgment debtors or parties assisting in enforcement, have, after lawfully imposing civil compulsory measures on such financial institutions and issuing decisions on fines or judicial detention, subsequently changed the subject at each level and imposed such measures on their superior financial institutions, up to the head office or parent company, and again issued decisions on fines or judicial detention, causing adverse impact. To correct this error, we hereby notify as follows:

1. In the enforcement process, when a people's court imposes civil compulsory measures on a financial institution that is a party assisting in enforcement, it shall decide strictly in accordance with the law and shall not change the subject at each level to hold its superior financial institution liable. According to Article 8 of the "Notice on Standardizing Court Enforcement and Financial Institution Assistance in Enforcement According to Law" (Fa Fa [2000] No. 21), jointly issued by this Court and the People's Bank of China on September 4, 2000, the following five conditions must be met for changing the subject at each level to hold a superior financial institution liable as a judgment debtor: (1) the financial institution must be a judgment debtor, and its debt must have been confirmed by an effective legal instrument; (2) the financial institution must have received a notice from the enforcement court requiring it to perform its debt repayment obligation within a period of fifteen days; (3) the financial institution must have failed to automatically perform its debt repayment obligation within the specified period, and the enforcement court must have attempted compulsory enforcement; (4) the financial institution must have failed to provide the enforcement court with property available for enforcement; and (5) the superior financial institution must bear joint and several liability for clearing the debt. The imposition of civil compulsory measures on a financial institution as a party assisting in enforcement due to its obstructive conduct is different from the situation where the financial institution is a judgment debtor. Therefore, the liability for judicial punishment shall be borne by the financial institution itself; changing the subject at each level to hold its superior financial institution liable for such punishment constitutes an error in the application of law.

2. In the enforcement process, if the subject has been lawfully changed at each level to hold a superior financial institution liable as a judgment debtor, and such superior financial institution engages in obstructive conduct while performing its debt repayment obligation, civil compulsory measures may be imposed on such superior financial institution. However, the people's court shall, in strict accordance with the provisions of Article 8 of the aforementioned notice, promptly issue a notice to the superior financial institution allowing it to automatically perform its debt repayment obligation within fifteen days, and shall not impose civil compulsory measures on it during the period for automatic performance.

3. The principle of fault liability shall be adhered to when imposing civil compulsory measures. Civil compulsory measures may be imposed on a financial institution only if its conduct is based on subjective intent and constitutes obstruction of enforcement; if the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability may also be pursued through legal procedures. Such civil compulsory measures and criminal penalties shall apply only to the actor at the financial institution that has intentionally fault, in order to fully reflect the punitive nature of national laws against illegal conduct.

4. If a financial institution disagrees with the decision of an enforcement court on civil compulsory measures, i.e., fines and judicial detention, it may, in accordance with Article 105 of the Civil Procedure Law, apply to the court at the next higher level for reconsideration; if a party submits a reconsideration application to the enforcement court, the enforcement court shall immediately forward it to the court at the next higher level and shall not withhold or delay transmission; after accepting the reconsideration application, the court at the next higher level shall promptly review and handle it; during the period when the court at the next higher level is reviewing the reconsideration application, the enforcement court may continue to execute the penalty decision, but if the court at the next higher level decides to revoke the penalty decision, the enforcement court shall immediately comply.

The above notice is to be conscientiously implemented by people's courts at all levels. Any circumstances or issues arising during implementation shall be promptly reported level by level to the Enforcement Work Office of this Court.

July 9, 2004
